messages:
alyssa: Heads-up: saw 3 OOMs on prod pool-B this morning during a ~30s traffic spike. Suspect mini-burst batch growth + pad blowup.

jordan: Which allocator trace? workspace or slab?

alyssa: workspace.reserve -> slab_alloc OOM. Seq lengths spiked to ~1024 from usual ~128, batch went 1->8 in a few seconds.

alyssa: Kernel switched to tiled-attn for the long seqs, which increased scratch WS per-token. KV cache also had old prefixes pinned so reuse didn't help.

miro: That combination rings a bell — kernel selection + sudden batch scaling can multiply workspace requests. Have you got perf counters? :thinking:

alyssa: Quick profiler dump attached inline:
```
alloc_timeline_ms: [0, 90, 115, 118, 121]
batch_size: [1,2,4,6,8]
avg_seq: [128,130,260,600,980]
ws_per_token_bytes: [64,64,64,256,256]
peak_request_mb: 8192
```

samira: Oof. tiled-attn switched ws_per_token 64->256 depending on kernel. That *alone* can 4x the reservation.

jordan: Any KV cache churn metrics? if old prefix entries stay pinned they prevent slab coalescing.

alyssa: KV cache eviction lag showed 12s tail; missed the burst window so buffers remained pinned.

miro: Proposed mitigations: 1) cap per-request pad growth (e.g., max_pad_multiplier=2) 2) quick-reclaim window for ephemeral KV entries 3) soft-fallback to smaller kernel when batch growth rate > threshold.

samira: Also consider a tiny proactive slab reserve for short bursts: reserve = ceil(avg_seq * batch * ws_per_token * 1.2) with a fast-return path.

jordan: + add a safety: if batch_delta_rate > X/sec then force serialize long sequences (or chunk) to avoid exponential alloc growth.

miro: We should also emit telemetry: batch_delta, pad_burn_bytes, per_seq_overhead so we can tune defaults. Right now we only see overall GPU mem.

alyssa: Agreed. I'll open a quick RFC for: (a) pad cap, (b) KV quick-reclaim, (c) kernel-fallback policy.

infra-bot: deploy 2026-03-12T06:10:00Z - prefetch-tweak rolled to pool-B (PR #4123). No relation to allocator change.

samira: For prototype I'll hack on a `fast_return` flag on the buffer pool that marks short-lived buffers reclaimable in <50ms. If it works we can land as opt-in.

alyssa: Thanks — would love a small dashboard panel showing pad_burn and per-seq WS so we can catch these spikes before OOMs.

jordan: I'll add a trace exporter for pad_burn and batch_growth rate, hook into alerting (SLO: pad_burn > 1GB in 60s -> page).

miro: One more thought: kernel selection heuristics could be smoothed (hysteresis) so a single long request doesn't flip kernels for entire batch. Helps avoid transient WS inflation.

alyssa: Good call. I'll note hysteresis + per-request kernel bucketing in the RFC.

samira: I'll prototype reserve heuristic tonight and post results. low-risk change first. :+1:

alyssa: Sweet. Thanks team — RFC incoming, will link updates here.
